overview: 2...f6 prepares ...e5 and ...Nge7 but weakens the king's diagonal and wastes time. White usually grabs the centre with Nf3 or Nc3 and d5 push, and Black's awkward set-up gives White a comfortable edge. Strong players avoid it.

white_ideas.idea: Take the centre with Nf3, Nc3 and push d5
Exploit the weak a2-g8 diagonal with Qh5+ ideas

typical_structures.structure: White pawns on e4 and d4 against ...f6

character.notes: Black has weakened the king and relies on the ...e5 break, so tactics around e5 and h5 can arise.

structure.notes: Black will break with ...e5, leaving a semi-open centre.

level.notes: Not a sound choice to learn.

character.reason: The weakened king and the ...e5 break make for early tactics.

gambit.reason: Material is level and no pawn is offered.

soundness.reason: ...f6 wastes time and weakens the king, giving White an easy edge.

structure.reason: White's e4/d4 centre faces a ...e5 break.

level.reason: A dubious defence is never Beginner and the ideas are simple.

plans.reason: White gets a big centre against a poorly placed Black set-up.
